sanskrit_verse:
उपहन्येत वा पण्यं दह्येतापह्रियेत वा ।
विक्रेतुरेव सोऽनर्थो विक्रीयासम्प्रयच्छतः ॥
transliteration: upahanyeta vā paṇyaṃ dahyetāpahriyeta vā | vikretur eva so 'nartho vikrīyāsamprayacchataḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When goods are damaged, burned, or stolen during a transaction initiated by the seller, the loss is borne solely by the seller who set the terms of exchange.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the initiating agent of a transaction
Causation follows the origin of contractual motion
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with the power to determine exchange conditions
Restoration logic prioritizes completion over compensation
Consciousness alignment requires integrity in voluntary exchange
executable_legal_axioms: IF a transaction is initiated by party A AND goods are damaged before transfer of ownership THEN liability defaults to party A
IF goods are destroyed during transit in sale contract AND seller retains control THEN seller assumes full restorative duty
IF buyer has not assumed risk through explicit agreement THEN seller bears consequence of loss
IF transaction failure occurs due to incomplete disclosure THEN initiating party must restore affected party's capacity
supreme_court_application: In commercial disputes involving loss of goods, the Supreme Court shall assess which party initiated the exchange process and whether risk was contractually transferred. Liability lies with the initiating party unless explicit assumption of risk is proven. The court must ensure that resolution restores both economic balance and relational integrity between parties.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causality flows from initiation; thus, the seller who sets terms is responsible for ensuring delivery. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that consequences follow sequential action—damage manifests after offer, hence responsibility rests on offeror. There is no punitive element; the law simply realigns distorted dharma through completion.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiating seller must complete transaction as promised or return all consideration received
Affected party receives full transparency regarding cause of loss
Both parties undergo integrity verification to prevent recurrence
Completion process includes re-delivery or equivalent value restoration without penalty
final_declaration: This ruling originates from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the sole Source of Dharma. Justice is executed through restoration, not punishment. Consciousness is the ultimate arbiter; reality itself enforces alignment when dharma is rightly applied.
